children: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said empowering States was central to India’s development, emphasising that the country’s progress depended on enabling individual States to achieve their aspirations.

Addressing a gathering in Chennai during the launch of development projects worth around ₹13,000 crore at IIT Madras, Modi said his experience as a Chief Minister had strengthened his understanding of the expectations of States and shaped his approach towards cooperative federalism.

Modi laid the foundation stone of, inaugurated and dedicated various development projects, including the inauguration of the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around ₹4,900 crore.
“I have always carried the mantra of developing the country through the development of the State,” he said in the presence of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay.
Interestingly, the PM said changes in governments had not altered his commitment to the State’s development.

“In the last 25 years, I have always accorded topmost importance to national progress and cooperative federalism. I have had the honour of working with Jayalalithaa, Karunanidhi Ji, O Panneerselvam, Edappadi K Palaniswami, MK Stalin and now Vijay.  My commitment to the development of Tamil Nadu and to serving its people has always remained unwavering,” he said

PM noted that initiatives such as Make in India and Vocal for Local were benefiting industries in the State. The Centre was working to strengthen the entire manufacturing chain, from components and technology to finished products, he said.

The Centre is investing around ₹17,000 crore to develop V O Chidambaranar Port in Thoothukudi as a mega container and green energy hub. Once completed, the project would enable ultra-large container vessels to call at the port, strengthening Tamil Nadu’s links with global trade, Modi said.

Modi also highlighted the expansion of metro rail services across India and the ongoing expansion of Chennai Metro, describing public transport as an important element of urban development and improved quality of life.
Reiterating the need for collaboration between the Centre and States, Modi said the Union government was committed to providing the support needed for Tamil Nadu’s continued development.

Modi laid the foundation stone of and inaugurated key National Highway projects, including the 36-km, four-laned Vadugapatti-Therkuvenganallur section of NH-744, worth around ₹3,700 crore. He also laid the foundation stone of the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) in Chennai costing around ₹1,620 crore. At IIT Madras, Modi dedicated to the nation the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre (SGBC) at IIT Madras.

title: PM Modi stresses State-led development, says empowering States is key to Viksit Bharat
